stem.en: Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu is dated to about 1.5 to 1.7 million years ago, and Isampur in Karnataka to 1.2 million years ago. What do these dates show?

text.en: Farming began in southern India more than a million years ago.

feedback.en: These are Palaeolithic sites of hunter-gatherers. Farming came far later, in the Neolithic.

text.en: People were using stone tools in southern India more than a million years ago.

feedback.en: A smaller number of years ago means more recent, so Isampur is the younger of the two.

text.en: The first humans in the world evolved in southern India.

feedback.en: Our earliest ancestors evolved in Africa. The oldest human settlement in the subcontinent dates to about 2 million years ago, well after that.

explanation.en: Both sites have large stone tools with animal fossils, and both dates are more than a million years ago. So people were using stone tools in southern India long before anyone farmed.

hints.en: Are these sites from the age of hunting or the age of farming?
